description: Browser-type plugin windows show somebody else's website, so this list is deliberately one command long. `browser_widget_control` is the only way such a page can touch its own window, and every call to it carries a token the host handed to the top frame at startup — the window setters are NOT granted here, because if they were, any script on the page could pin, resize or hide the window without a token and the token would be decoration. No plugin-host, no file access, no vault, no activity data, no LLM key. The `remote` list is deliberately SHORTER than the manifest's allowedOrigins: navigating to a login provider has to work, but a login provider has no business holding the control bridge, so it can be reached and cannot call anything. The `plugin.` entries are this app's own protocol handler under the URL Windows actually gives it — see the test in src/plugin/mod.rs.
